title: BlissCam: Boosting Eye Tracking Efficiency with Learned In-Sensor Sparse Sampling
problem: Eye tracking systems suffer from long end-to-end tracking latency and high power consumption, consuming up to half the power budget of mobile VR devices. Existing optimization efforts focus exclusively on the computation pipeline while ignoring the image sensor front-end.
motivation: Eye tracking is increasingly critical for emerging AR/VR platforms, making power and latency reduction essential for practical mobile VR deployment.
method: BlissCam reduces pixels 20x by using machine learning to select important pixels directly within the image sensor hardware. Custom circuitry added to the sensor's existing pixel readout chains performs this learned filtering at the hardware level. This cuts both sensor power consumption and data transmission to the host, lowering computation and memory bandwidth demands on the receiving computer.
key_novelty: The core idea is applying learned pixel selection (machine learning to pick important pixels) directly on the sensor hardware rather than the host computer.
contributions: Introduced the paradigm of in-sensor sparse sampling for eye tracking systems
Designed BlissCam hardware achieving 20x pixel downsampling within the sensor with minimal augmentation to existing pixel circuitry
Achieved 8.2x energy reduction and 1.4x latency reduction over existing eye tracking pipelines
Demonstrated practical sensor-level optimization reducing both readout power and sensor-host communication overhead
limitations: Trade-offs between learned sparse sampling quality and eye tracking accuracy are not explicitly discussed.
primary_theme: In-sensor sparse sampling for efficient eye tracking
